title: LRU cache
summary: O(1) get and put with a hash map into a doubly linked list: splice to promote, evict from the back, then the follow-ups interviewers ask.

clips.title: Hash map + linked list
clips.question: Design an LRU cache where get and put are both O(1).

scenes.say: LRU cache, problem one. Design a least recently used cache, where both get and put run in constant time. Pause and answer out loud.

props.question: An LRU cache with O(1) get and put?

scenes.say: Pair a hash map with a doubly linked list. The list keeps keys in recency order: most recent at the front, least recent at the back. The map points from each key straight to its list node. With capacity two: put one, then put two. Each new key goes in at the front. Get one: the map finds its node, and splice moves it to the front, without allocating. Put three: the cache is full, so evict from the back, key two, erasing it from the map too. Then three goes in at the front. Now get two misses, and returns minus one.

steps.note: New key → node at the front
put(2): front again; key 1 shifts back
get(1): splice its node to the front, O(1)
Full: evict the back (key 2) from list and map

clips.title: Your turn: the code
clips.question: Write LRUCache with get and put.

scenes.say: Your turn. With a std list and an unordered map, write the LRU cache class, with get and put. Pause and write it yourself.

props.question: Write LRUCache: get and put, both O(1).
props.label: Your turn

scenes.say: Here is one solution. The list holds key value pairs, front most recent, and the map holds iterators into it. Get returns minus one on a miss. On a hit, splice moves the node to the front in constant time. Put on an existing key updates the value and splices it forward. When the cache is full, erase the back key from the map first, then pop the back node. Finally, emplace the new pair at the front, and store its iterator.

props.title: LRUCache, one solution

highlights.note: list = recency order; map = key → node
Evict: map entry first, then the node
Insert at the front, remember it

scenes.say: Four classic bugs. Storing an index instead of an iterator in the map makes promotion linear. Forgetting to erase the map entry on eviction leaves stale keys. Popping the back before reading its key loses it. And skipping the existing-key case in put creates duplicate nodes.

items.label: Eviction
items.title: Erase the map entry
items.body: Or size() and lookups go stale.

items.label: put()
items.title: Existing keys
items.body: Update and promote; don't insert twice.

clips.title: Follow-ups
clips.question: Why a doubly linked list, can get take a shared lock, and how would you build LFU?

scenes.say: Problem three, the follow-ups. Why a doubly linked list? Can get take a shared lock? And how would you build least frequently used instead? Pause and answer out loud.

props.question: Why doubly linked, can get share a lock, and what about LFU?

scenes.say: Common follow-ups. Why doubly linked? To unlink a node you need its predecessor, which a singly linked list can't give you in constant time. Why is splice constant time? It relinks a few pointers, with no allocation. Can get take a shared lock? No: it reorders the list, so even reads need an exclusive lock. And to add expiry, store a deadline per entry, and treat expired entries as misses.

items.label: Doubly linked
items.title: O(1) unlink
items.body: Removing a node needs its predecessor.

items.label: Threads
items.title: Exclusive lock
items.body: get() reorders the list: it is a write.

scenes.say: If they ask for least frequently used instead: keep one list per access count, plus the current minimum count. Get and put stay constant time, but brand new keys get evicted quickly, before they can build up a count.

left.label: LRU
left.title: Recency
left.code:
list<pair<K, V>> list_;
unordered_map<K, iter> map_;
left.body: One list, one map. Evicts the least recently used.

right.label: LFU
right.title: Frequency
right.body: A list per count; evict from freqMap[minFreq].

verdict.text: LFU suits skewed, repeated access; new keys die young.

scenes.say: To recap. A hash map points into a doubly linked list in recency order. Get splices the node to the front. Put evicts from the back when full, erasing the map entry first. And get is a write, so it needs an exclusive lock.

items.text: Hash map → nodes of a recency list.
get splices the node to the front.
put evicts the back; erase the map entry first.
get is a write: exclusive lock.
